text:
Noah D.: running into another TS/ESM edge oddity. Quickstart sample typechecks locally but Vercel Edge deploy fails with "No overload matches this call" when using createClient<T>.
Noah D.: repro: Next Edge API route, import style `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` then `const c = Redwood.createClient<{user: string}>({})`. Local tsc OK, remote build fails.
Priya S.: that pattern rings a bell. Is the SDK publishing a single flattened d.ts and using `export default` for createClient?
Noah D.: yep, dist/types/index.d.ts has default export overloads. package.json has conditional exports but only a single types entry at the top-level.
Vera K.: edge runtimes + bundlers can resolve types differently. Two practical approaches: tighten the overloads/generics so TS can pick the right signature, and make types resolution explicit for ESM viewers.
Priya S.: example of making overloads less ambiguous:
```ts
export function createClient<T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(opts: Opts): Client<T>;
export function createClient<T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>>(opts: Opts, hooks: Hooks<T>): Client<T>;
export default createClient;
```
Priya S.: avoid `= any` for the generic default. `any` weakens inference and can cause the compiler to match the wrong overload.
Noah D.: ok, try that. But what about the import ambiguity? consumers still do `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'`.
Vera K.: prefer named exports for the factory in types: `export function createClient...` then also `export default createClient;` as a runtime-friendly default. That reduces `typeof import("...").default` vs named symbol confusion.
Noah D.: pkg exports atm:
```json
"type": "module",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
Vera K.: change to conditional types so ESM consumers see matching declarations:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/types/esm/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Vera K.: publish both dist/types/esm and dist/types/cjs. TS will prefer the `types` field under the chosen export condition.
Priya S.: also add a short README note for edge users: suggest `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` or include an example tsconfig snippet:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
Priya S.: `moduleResolution: "bundler"` helps modern toolchains (Vercel, Bun) pick the right type entry. For older setups `nodeNext` can be appropriate.
Noah D.: any test/CI catch we can add to avoid regressions?
Vera K.: add a smoke consumer in CI that does `npm pack` the SDK, extracts it, and runs `tsc` against a tiny consumer with both `nodeNext` and `bundler` configs. Also verify both `import default` and named-import forms typecheck.
build-bot: opened issue #1368: "sdk: edge quickstart - overload/type resolution failures" assigned to @noahd
Noah D.: I'll draft a PR with: 1) tighten generic defaults, 2) prefer named exports in d.ts with default delegator, 3) conditional types in exports, 4) README tsconfig example, 5) CI consumer tsc job. ETA tomorrow morning.
Priya S.: happy to review declaration output. Also consider making one overload accept an options object with a `hooks?` property rather than a second positional param; discriminator avoids overlap.
Vera K.: yep that plus explicit discriminant shapes reduces ambiguity even more. Thanks team.
Noah D.: thanks all :rocket:
